To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a paper directory for a mobile phone network can be an effective information service that facilitates search and increases communication on the network, and that (2) such a directory is a public good that generates both productive and distributives benefits for the network.

the provision of a complementary information service for mobile phones, and its impact on the use of the mobile phone network, and on the welfare of both sides of the network.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mobile phones are a very important part of the information infrastructure of developing countries, but that they are not yet a complete information infrastructure.
information services that facilitate communication on mobile phone networks can have large impacts, but they are likely to be public goods.
the benefits of mobile phones are substantially enhanced by the availability of information services that allow search on the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
information services are a critical complement to mobile phones in developing countries.
information services can play a critical role in expanding the use of mobile phones, especially among the poorest and least educated.
the provision of complementary information services to facilitate search on mobile networks can generate substantial economic benefits, but these services will often be under-provided by the market.
